title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
lede: An analysis of released weights claims China's leading open-weight models, including DeepSeek V4 and Moonshot's Kimi K3, show signs of training on Nvidia Blackwell GPUs that the US bars from export to China.

points: Will DePue of the nonprofit Unemployment Labs examined open weights released by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group.
He argues the weights retain traces of the hardware that trained them, and those traces point to Blackwell chips.
That does not prove a violation: the chips could sit in offshore data centers such as Malaysia's, a route China hawks want closed.
Epoch AI estimates about two million advanced chips reached China in 2024 and 2025 through schemes that hid their destination.
It lands days after Huang left Nvidia over his relationship with Alice Huang of Megaspeed, a firm implicated in chip smuggling.

sections.text: If weights reveal the hardware behind them, provenance becomes checkable from released files, and pressure grows for export rules that govern who uses chips rather than where they are shipped.
